recipes.name: Pork, Apple, and Ginger Stir-Fry with Hoisin Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 pound pork loin, sliced and cut into thin strips

steps.text: Whisk together the hoisin sauce, brown sugar, soy sauce, and applesauce in a small bowl; set aside.
Combine the pork and cornstarch in a bowl. Mix until the cornstarch evenly coats the pork; set aside.

Heat the peanut oil and sesame oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Cook the pork in three separate batches in the hot oil until no longer pink in the middle, 2 to 3 minutes per batch. Remove pork to a plate lined with paper towels to drain, reserving the oil. Add the ginger to the skillet; cook and stir for 30 seconds. Stir in the broccoli and cook until tender. Return the pork to the skillet and pour in the sauce; toss to coat. Cook until all ingredients are hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Pork, Apple, and Ginger Stir-Fry with Hoisin Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This simple stir-fry has a sweet taste that appeals to teenagers. While broccoli is specified here, it's easy to add whatever vegetables you have available to it. Serve this over rice for a filling meal.

review.reviewBody:
I did a pared down, lighter-on-the-calories version of this and it was spectacular. I used 1 tbsp of olive oil supplemented with olive oil cooking spray rather than the peanut and sesame oils. I left out the cornstarch and just cooked the pork in the olive oil. I didn't have broccoli, so I used a green pepper, a red pepper, and an onion, all sliced. Oh, and I had 1.5 pounds of pork tenderloin, so I used it all. 

I left the sauce unchanged (except used splenda brown sugar blend instead of brown sugar); it is delicious as written. My husband loved it even though he doesn't normally like sweet foods, and our three male guests raved about it.

I served it with a basic fried rice (3 cups cooked white rice, 1 egg, 3 tablespoons each of soy sauce and rice vinegar, all fried up together with olive oil).

I just finished this for dinner, and it was sooo good! I threw in some fresh sliced mushrooms and some sliced onion. Okay, okay, I made some other changes, but I don’t feel they compromised the original recipe. Because I don’t eat pork, I used sliced boneless chicken breast; I whisked 1.5 tsp. of ground ginger into the sauce (I had no fresh ginger); and I grated one Cortland apple into the sauce in place of the applesauce, which I also didn’t have. And let me say one thing about velveting chicken with cornstarch, which I had never done before: do it—it made the most tender chicken I have ever eaten. Try this recipe as is or with these changes, and you won’t be disappointed. So good!

I'll admit I was skeptical of the apple sauce in the stir fry sauce but it works! I didn't make the recipe exactly as written just because I doubled it and didn't have quite enough ginger, I added minced garlic, used 1.5 times the sugar and didn't quite double the soy sauce because I'm always scared of it being too salty. (My daughter says I must have a salt sensitivity!) I put a bit of cornstarch in with the sauce and just sautéed the pork in a little bit of canola oil without dredging it. I also added a squirt of siracha to the sauce. The heat was good with the sweet. Oh, and I added three sliced carrots. So, it's a versatile recipe. It was very yummy!

I’ll be making this again. Made as written (substituting the broccoli with carrots, red pepper and snap peas), tasted great! The single ingredient I added was some Chinese 5 spice on the pork before adding the cornstarch. Has great flavour, not too sweet but would maybe consider adding something with a little heat next time. I served with ramen, mixing it in to coat with sauce.

I like this recipe a lot and do not think it is too sweet. I don't ever have hoisin sauce on hand so I have omitted it both times I've made it. (Maybe that's why it's not overly sweet) I also grate my ginger instead of chop it. I think it helps the ginger dissolve into the dish so you don't bite into pieces of ginger (yuck), you just get a nice ginger flavor throughout the sauce. I like the applesauce in the sauce as a thickener, so I didn't have to thicken it with any cornstarch.

Yum! I didn't have any hoisin sauce, but I made some using cashew butter instead of peanut butter; used tamari instead of soy sauce; and used canola oil instead of peanut oil (all changes due to hubby's dietary restrictions). It took me longer than the recipe said to get the pork hot enough, but I think I may have not cooked it long enough the first round. Served this mixed up with rice noodles. We have a new "comfort food"!

I forgot to get apple sauce at the store so I just put a peeled red apple in the blender and used that. The recipe turned out awesome! In fact, my husband had to take some in a container for the road and he actually called me just to tell me how much he loved it!
Really good. Made it with brussels sprouts, carrots and mushrooms and stir fried with boiled ramen noodles like others suggested. I halved the soy sauce and halved the sugar.

The flavors of this dish are great, but it's pretty heavy on the soy sauce. I halved it and still needed to add a little water at the end to mellow it out (almost took the rating down to a 3, but I think this recipe idea is worth keeping, so I'm being generous). The hoisin and ginger are awesome, plus I added black pepper and some chili flakes. I used a raw stir-fry mix of broccoli, carrots and snow peas. Yum! Thanks for the recipe!

I was skeptical about making this but I am glad I did. I used unsweetened apple sauce and didn't find it overly sweet as did some other reviewers. I did add a bit of garlic too. It was great, nicely spiced and will be my go to sauce for stir-frying other things like chicken too.

Great recipe for the the whole family. I added a chopped onion, half a green bell pepper, sliced, 1 can each of bamboo shoots and water chestnuts, drained. I doubled the ingrediants for the sauce to compensate for the extra veggies. My husband and kids raved throughout dinner. They were all shocked to find out that it had applesauce in the recipe. Will fix again.
One of my fave stir fry's to make!
Husband loved it, I little sweet for me but I’ll adjust next time.
Good flavor but didn't like the texture that applesauce added.

Really liked this! Quick, easy, and oh so tasty! Followed the recipe as written. The only thing I'll do differently next time is to reduce the sriracha sauce since it was a too spicy for my mother. Even so she really liked the flavor so it goes in the rotation.
Great flavour. Add a tablespoon or two of chilli sauce.
Delicious!

My husband and I both loved this dish. Is definitely a unique take on oriental flavors. A bit salty for me but unsure if it was this dish or the Asian quinoa I had with it. I used a mix of broccoli, baby carrots, and snap peas for veggie variety. Will make again and probably throw in some water chestnuts and mushrooms next time.
Awesome almost exactly as written. I just cut down on the soy sauce and added onions, mushrooms and peppers. Easy and very tasty.
I think next time I will make this with 1/3 as much soy sauce as the recipe calls for. Too salty for me but my boyfriend loved it!
